content:
rachel_ae: Heads-up — Kestrel Analytics renewal due Nov 15. Their traffic doubled after ML pipeline launch. They asked to rebaseline commit and want a short-term uplift protection.

dan_dealdesk: what's their current commit + term? Any historical overage patterns?

rachel_ae: Current: $40k/mo, 12 months. Last 3 months avg usage ~$95k/mo. They want to avoid surprise invoices and asked for a 6-month buffer with a cap at +25% of their new baseline.

priya_se: tech note: we migrated two heavy scoring jobs to dedicated GPUs in July which explains the spike. If they enable batch windowing and token compression we can cut token spend by ~15%. Worth proposing as part of the renewal.

emily_custsuc: customer asked explicitly for: 1) stepped commit, 2) an overage cap, 3) a one-time credit to offset migration costs (estimated $20k). They also want a trial of Dedicated for an extra endpoint for 60 days.

tom_fin: high level: we can do stepped commit, but discounts and credits need to stay within margin guardrails. Any effective discount > 18% -> exec approval. Need blended margin calc.

dan_dealdesk: propose options: A) Stepped commit: 60k/mo (3mo) -> 85k/mo (9mo); $20k credit amortized over first 4 invoices; overage capped at 15% with 5% discounted rate. B) Fixed 80k/mo for 12mo with $20k up-front credit and no overage cap but 10% discount on overage. Which looks better margin-wise?

priya_se: Option A is safer for customer predictability. Also add a runbook: if Dedicated trial fails perf targets (p95 < 200ms) within 60 days, we'll roll them back and provide month credit.

rachel_ae: customer prefers Option A but wants the overage cap at 25% not 15%. They argue growth could continue.

tom_fin: 25% cap increases risk. If we accept 25% we need to increase the commit floor or shorten the stepped period. Suggest: 70k/mo (2mo) -> 95k/mo (10mo) with the 25% cap, credit amortized over 3 invoices. That improves visibility on ARR.

d an_dealdesk: @legal_bot can we add a clause that caps our liability for rollback and defines overage calculation by "billable tokens" with logger retention for auditing?

legal_bot: no legal blocking issues. Recommend precise definitions: "Billable tokens = total tokens processed excluding server-side compression and cache hits"; include audit option where customer can request token logs within 30 days. Also clarify credit application timing.

deploy_bot: deployment note: Dedicated trial provisioning lead time ~7 business days; need signed addendum to schedule.

emily_custsuc: customer asks for an escape if costs > 150% of commit in any single month during first 6 months. Can we add a one-time true-up right?

priya_se: technical rollback path ok, but true-up language needs to be concrete. We can offer one-time true-up option to renegotiate commit if monthly spend >150% of commit for 2 consecutive months. Must require 30-day notice.

tom_fin: that works, but any true-up that reduces ARR needs to be escalated. Add contingency for transitional credits.

dan_dealdesk: summary for approvals: selected concession set = stepped commit (70k x2mo -> 95k x10mo), $20k credit amortized over 3 invoices, overage cap 25% at 5% discounted overage rate, Dedicated 60-day trial, rollback SLA + one-time true-up trigger. Estimated net effective discount ~14% per our model. Need final sign-off from Finance.

rachel_ae: I'll share these terms with Kestrel today and ask for verbal OK. Can Deal Desk route for approval once Finance OKs?

tom_fin: approving to route to Deal Desk for exec review. I'll finish the blended margin calc and post in here by EOD.

dan_dealdesk: routing to Finance and Revenue Ops now. If approved I'll upload redlines and ask Legal to prep the addendum.

emily_custsuc: I'll prep migration plan and customer comms for the trial window.

rachel_ae: thanks all — customer asked for final terms by EOD Thursday. We should be able to hit that timeline if Finance posts calc today. :rocket:
